task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 10, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer about the Juniper Arch music room's membership experiment, answering what subscribers buy and how their attendance changes the economics for the venue and performers.

facts.text: Juniper Arch music room began a monthly membership program in May 2026 and published its first operating review in August.
Membership costs $18 a month and includes admission to two eligible regular shows during that month.
A normal ticket to one of those shows costs $12, making two separate admissions $24.
A member attending two eligible shows pays $6 less than buying two ordinary tickets; a member attending none still pays $18.
Unused admissions do not roll over into the next month.
Special touring shows are excluded and require separately purchased tickets.
Membership does not guarantee a place at a particular sold-out show; reservations are required.
The 80-seat venue initially reserves 20 places per regular show for members and releases unused member places to general sale 48 hours before the performance.
There were 240 full-fee memberships in July, producing $4,320 in membership receipts for that month.
The venue does not receive another $18 each time a member attends; the attendance uses an existing monthly entitlement.
Each redeemed member admission triggers a $4 allocation to that show's artist-payment account.
Membership receipts also support room rental and administration, so they are not all paid to performers.
Manager Olla Fenn says recurring receipts help schedule shows before all tickets are sold, while high redemption increases event costs.
Fenn said, "A predictable payment is useful, but an occupied seat still has a cost attached."
Member Ceri Vale works irregular shifts and has used both admissions in one month and none in another.
Vale said, "The value depends on whether my free nights match the music, not just how many shows are on the calendar."
The review does not publish a final profit comparison with an otherwise identical season without memberships.
Members can cancel future months through the venue office; the current month's payment is not automatically prorated for unused visits.
The music room occupies an upstairs former meeting hall and presents mostly acoustic acts.
Drinks, merchandise and the excluded touring shows are outside the two-admission benefit.

forbidden_additions: Unlimited entry, guaranteed seats or rollover of unused admissions
All membership receipts go to artists or the trial has proved a profit increase
